name: Catherine Ann Ware Warfield
bio: Catherine Ann Ware Warfield (1816–1877) was an American poet and novelist from Mississippi and Kentucky. Eggleston prints her as Catherine M. Warfield; her Manassas celebrates the first Confederate victory of the Civil War.
The poems here are taken from American War Ballads and Lyrics, edited by George Cary Eggleston (New York and London: G. P. Putnam’s Sons, 1889), where it is printed under his or her name: Manassas.

poems.title: Manassas
poems.author: Catherine Ann Ware Warfield
poems.text:
They have met at last--as storm-clouds
          Meet in heaven,
And the Northmen back and bleeding
          Have been driven:
And their thunders have been stilled,
And their leaders crushed or killed,
And their ranks with terror thrilled,
          Rent and riven!

Like the leaves of Vallambrosa
          They are lying;
In the moonlight, in the midnight,
          Dead and dying:
Like those leaves before the gale,
Swept their legions, wild and pale;
While the host that made them quail
          Stood, defying.

When aloft in morning sunlight
        Flags were flaunted,
And "swift vengeance on the rebel"
        Proudly vaunted:
Little did they think that night
Should close upon their shameful flight,
And rebels, victors in the fight,
        Stand undaunted.

But peace to those who perished
        In our passes!
Light be the earth above them;
        Green the grasses!
Long shall Northmen rue the day
When they met our stern array,
And shrunk from battle's wild affray
        At Manassas.
